en: The Questions of Milinda,
Great Chapter 3:
The Chapter on Investigation (Vīmaṁsanapañha)
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, will you converse with me?
"Great King, if you will converse according to the way of the wise, I shall converse; but if you will converse according to the way of kings, I shall not converse."
“How, venerable Nāgasena, do the wise converse?
“In the conversation of the wise, O Great King, there is wrapping up,
there is unraveling, there is refutation, there is counter-argument, there is trust, and there is mutual trust.”
“Furthermore, the wise do not become angry because of that; it is in this way, Great King, that the wise converse.
“But how, venerable sir, do kings converse?

“Great King, in conversation, kings acknowledge a single premise. To whoever contradicts that premise, they issue a command for punishment, saying, ‘Inflict punishment upon this person! It is in this way, Great King, that kings converse.”
“Venerable sir, I shall converse with you as a scholar speaks, not as a king speaks.
Let the Blessed One speak freely, just as he would when conversing with a bhikkhu, a novice, a lay follower, or a monastery attendant;
let the Blessed One speak freely and do not be afraid.”
“Very well, Great King,” the Elder replied in approval.
The king said,
“Venerable Nāgasena, I shall ask a question.”
“Ask, Great King,” [he said].
“I have asked you, Bhante,” [the king replied].
“It has been answered, Great King,” [he said].
“But what, venerable sir, have you answered?
“But what, great king, have you asked?
This was the third question for investigation.
